shortDescription: Russia's state-controlled leading tanker group Sovcomflot RUS:FLOT expects a significant improvement to its financial results in 2026 and 2027, supported by favourable global market conditions, its CEO told the Kommersant newspaper, following a 2025 loss.

children: Russia's state-controlled leading tanker group Sovcomflot
expects a significant improvement to its financial results in 2026 and 2027, supported by favourable global market conditions, its CEO told the Kommersant newspaper, following a 2025 loss.

Western sanctions imposed on Sovcomflot and its fleet in the past few years to reduce Russia's oil revenues were a key factor behind the company's $648.4 million net loss in 2025 compared with a $424 million net profit in 2024
"We expect to double EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation) in 2026 compared with 2025," CEO Igor Tonkovidov said
"In terms of net profit, we have returned to a sustainable positive result comparable to 2024", he added
this year has disrupted the tanker market and created a capacity shortage, resulting in higher freight rates, he said

"The profitability of transporting Russian crude oil and petroleum products in 2026 has been somewhat lower than in the global market because the Russian segment has been operating under severe sanctions pressure for a fifth consecutive year," Tonkovidov told the paper

Sovcomflot also expects the market to remain "fairly strong" in 2027, partially due to global market conditions and partially because of a growing contracted revenue backlog, which exceeds $14 billion compared with $6 billion two years ago
Next year would be financially stable for Sovcomflot "under any circumstances" thanks to its contracted revenue, Tonkovidov said
